notes: Strong semantic control and compact output; labor-heavy for perspective-rich scenes and changed-view variants. Requires scene manifest and independent accidental-hazard review rather than relying on illustrator memory.
Best default for planar/simple rooms and object arrangements. Component reuse improves controlled variants and provenance, but a scene must not become a location-memorization template.

method: Blender/procedural 3D blocking plus deterministic line/static render
notes: Excellent camera/occlusion/mechanical control and transfer variants. Freestyle/static rendering is supported by current Blender; people, cloth, spills, clutter, and an exam-like hand-drawn finish may need cleanup.

Retains 3D layout authority while allowing readable people/organic forms and restrained line character. Cleanup must be constrained: any silhouette/object/condition change triggers semantic re-review and hotspot regeneration.
Good for complex human poses and organic scenes if commissioned under explicit rights terms. Lowest deterministic transfer/rebuild leverage unless anchored to project-owned blocking and manifest.

Prompt/seed/model pinning does not guarantee cross-platform/release reproducibility, and free-form generation can invent objects, conditions, text, geometry, or hazards. Review burden defeats its apparent generation speed for scored safety scenes.

method: controlled image-to-image from project-owned depth/segmentation/render inputs
notes: Structural controls improve guidance but do not guarantee preservation. May be tested only as a stylistic derivative with exact model/input hashes, strict structural gates, independent review, and the deterministic pre-generation render retained as controlling fallback.

Route simple scenes to modular SVG; geometry/occlusion scenes to deterministic 3D blocking; use constrained human cleanup/illustration for soft or human forms. One semantic scene contract, QA ontology, versioning model, and deterministic manifest spans every route.
